notes: A clean six-bullet page and the ladder follows it almost one-to-one. The only judgement calls: bullet 3 ('go to Carpenters' Landing where you will fight an Orc NM') is a journey plus a preview of bullet 4, so it carries no step of its own -- its two sub-bullets are zone-entry routing and fold into the ??? step's note. Bullet 5 is TWO actions in one sentence, the kill and the second touch, so it splits; the Red oil key item comes from the second touch, which is why the evidence sits on the examine and not on the fight. Red oil is a key item (id 704) and is NOT the header's reward -- the reward is Mannequin Pumps -- so using it as evidence is clean. The final talk carries the Red oil as items rather than evidence: it is what you must be holding to hand in. The ??? resolves as an object with no marker key, so steps 3 and 5 keep their rungs and lose their markers, which is the expected cost of a ???.

notes:
Three bullets, but bullet 2 is two NPCs in two different cities and bullet 3 is two different things, so the ladder is five rungs. The two briefings are an unordered set -- the page lists them as peers and the sub-bullet only insists both be started before any Voidwatch NM dies -- so they share a group and both draw at once. Step 4 ('complete both subquests') is a real thing the player must do and is kept as an unmarkable rung -- the two VW Op quests are separate quests with their own pages and nothing here can track them. 'Quest Reqs: Adventurer's Certificate' is a key-item prerequisite with no slot in the schema; 'Level 75 or higher' from the same field is a plain level gate and is recorded as one, even though the header's own Level row is empty. VERIFY: the draft put the Ashen stratum abyssite on step 1 as evidence, on the strength of bullet 1 saying Kieran hands it over at the start, and flagged that it was breaking hard rule 7 to do it. It is verbatim the header's Reward line, so the evidence is removed and the quest now has no observable at all -- nothing advances this ladder and it will sit on Kieran until a human overrides it. That is the deliberate cost of the rule; if the walkthrough is judged to beat the header here, step 1 is where the abyssite goes back. CORRECTION: hard rule 7 has since been rewritten so that a reward IS evidence when the walkthrough hands it over before the last bullet, and this is exactly that case -- bullet 1 of 3 gives you the Ashen stratum abyssite -- so it is restored as step 1's evidence and the ladder has an observable again.

notes: Four bullets, two steps. Bullet 3 (farm from Funguars, Saplings, Goblin Thugs or gardening, or buy at the Auction House, and avoid Wild Onions because cooks bid them up) is shopping advice, and bullet 4 is a repeat cooldown -- neither is a step. The three-way OR is the whole quest and it models exactly: Sleepshroom as the AND-list, Treant Bulb and Wild Onion as the two alternatives. The time of day does NOT gate completion -- the page says a mismatched item still completes it for 100g -- so nothing here is time-gated in the sense that would need flagging; the windows are recorded in the step note only. No evidence: the reward is gil, and holding one of the three mushrooms is readiness for the trade, not proof of a completed step. The NPC has no zone in the walkthrough at all; Bastok Markets (L-8) comes from the header's Start line.

notes: Five bullets, five steps, and the good news is that 'Song Runes' is a real markable entity rather than a ???, so the last two rungs both carry a marker. The line above the walkthrough -- 'This quest will not appear on your quest list until completion' -- is not a step but it matters to the runtime, so it is flagged: anything that reads quest status from the log will never see this one in progress, and the item ladder is the only handle there is. The Parchment obtain step keeps its evidence, following the pilot's Operation Teatime precedent, but it is the weakest evidence in this batch: Parchment is an ordinary Leathercraft material, so a player who already owns one starts the ladder at the Song Runes and never sees the Bki Tbujhja marker. notes: Six bullets and only three of them are things you do. Bullet 2 is what happens when you talk to Chululu, not a separate action, so it folds into step 1; bullet 5 (another random card per real-life day) is a cooldown; bullet 6 is a pointer at the follow-on quest All in the Cards. The five random cards from bullet 2 are deliberately NOT evidence: which of the four you get is random and unobservable in advance, and an alt-list over all four would collide with step 2's AND-list over the same four items, which the duplicate gate rejects outright and which would jump the mark to the hand-in the moment you got your first stack. So the one evidence point is 'you hold one of each', on the collecting step, and it lands the marker on Chululu exactly when you are ready to hand in. All four card names resolve as items (558, 559, 561, 562). The reward is 'Fortunetelling...', which is not an item at all.
